company_name: The PNC Financial Services Group, Inc.
model: Bank FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route; GAAP earnings after regulatory capital retention, preferred stock deducted in the equity bridge, net debt zero)

equity_bridge.item: Preferred stock (Series B, T, U, V, W, X; carrying value after the Series S redemption)
equity_bridge.note: Capital surplus - preferred stock $5,882m at 30 Sep 2026 (Q3 2026 10-Q equity statement; Tier 1 table 5,881) less the $525m Series S redeemed at par on 1 Nov 2026 (Note 17 Subsequent Events). Dividends ~$290m/yr after the redemption (Q3 2026 $73m incl. Series S). Deducted at book because the flows are total net income before preferred dividends; at a ~5.5% average coupon versus a 10.5% cost of equity, book over-states the economic claim by ~$1.5bn (~$4/share) -- conservative, consistent with HBAN/NTRS.

equity_bridge.item: Cash paid to redeem Series S preferred on 1 Nov 2026 (after the 30 Sep balance sheet)
equity_bridge.note: The redemption left as cash after the balance-sheet date and before the first modelled flow (FY2027), so it is deducted to keep the event value-neutral, as the prior version judged it: preferred falls $525m and so do the assets behind common equity. CET1 is unaffected (preferred is additional Tier 1); Tier 1 falls ~0.1pt from 11.0%.

historical_growth.fcf_series_note: For a bank the distributable-earnings series is GAAP net income (already after share-based compensation): FY2020 7,558 (incl. ~$4.3bn after-tax gain on the BlackRock stake sale in discontinued operations, offset by a COVID CECL build); FY2021 5,725 (BBVA USA merger costs); FY2022 6,113; FY2023 5,647; FY2024 5,953; FY2025 6,997 (SEC XBRL ProfitLoss). 3-year CAGR 4.6%, 5-year -1.5% (distorted by the FY2020 BlackRock gain). Revenue (us-gaap:Revenues = NII + noninterest income): FY2020 16,901; FY2022 21,120; FY2025 23,099 -- the 5-year 6.5% is inflated by BBVA USA (closed June 2021); the 3-year 3.0% spans the 2023-24 deposit-repricing trough. Diluted EPS FY2020 16.99 (BlackRock gain), FY2022 13.85, FY2025 16.59. Equity (total equity incl. NCI): FY2020 54,041; FY2022 45,812 (AOCI trough); FY2025 60,636.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Base-case 10-year average revenue growth (6.5% FY27 tapering to 2.5%), bracketed by the 3-year revenue CAGR (3.0%, a deposit-repricing trough window) and the 5-year (6.5%, BBVA-inflated). Equity CAGRs are AOCI swings and acquisition issuance, not compounding.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3-year CAGR (9.8%) diverges >30% from revenue (3.0%) and the 5-year (2.3%) from revenue (6.5%): FY2022 book value was depressed by ~$10bn of unrealised AFS losses in AOCI that have since partly unwound, so the 3-year equity CAGR measures AOCI recovery, and the 5-year starts from the post-BlackRock-sale FY2020 peak before the BBVA cash purchase. EPS 5-year is negative only because FY2020 includes the BlackRock gain. Growth is taken from the revenue series and FY2026-27 guidance.

scenario_narratives.base: PNC has banked the FirstBank conversion and is growing loans much faster than expected (average loans +2% in Q3 2026, +2.5% guided for Q4), which carries net interest income up ~15.5% in FY2026 even though the margin slipped to 2.94% in Q3. Revenue grows ~6.5% in FY2027 fading to 2.5%. Costs are running hotter than first modelled (FY2026 core expense guidance raised to +9.5%), so the efficiency ratio reaches ~55% a year later than before, by FY2029, while provisions normalise from today's ~24-27bp charge-off rate to ~33bp mid-cycle. Faster loan growth also means more capital kept back in FY2027 with CET1 at 9.8%. GAAP EPS reaches ~$21.45 in FY2027 (vs ~$19 in FY2026), and ~70-85% of earnings are distributed. At a 10.5% cost of equity that franchise is worth ~2.2x tangible book (~11x FY2027E EPS), against the ~2.05x the market pays.
scenario_narratives.bull: NIM recovers and reaches ~3.20% as fixed-rate assets reprice into 5% long rates, the Sunbelt/Mountain West franchises take deposit share, capital markets compound toward the 25-30% target and positive operating leverage takes efficiency to ~52.5% by FY2030 from a Q4 2026 starting point near 57%. Credit stays benign (~28bp). ROTCE reaches ~20%, EPS compounds high-single-digit, and PNC earns a money-centre-like multiple of tangible book.
scenario_narratives.bear: NIM stalls around the 2.94% printed in Q3 2026 as new lending comes on at thinner spreads and deposit competition keeps funding costs sticky; loan growth stalls and the 2026 capital-markets pull-forward reverses. Office CRE stress (28% criticized, 11% nonperforming) spreads into the wider CRE book and a mid-sized credit cycle takes provisions to ~70bp in FY2028. Efficiency stays near 58%, ROTCE settles at 13-15% (a thin spread over a 10.5% cost of equity), and with CET1 at 9.8% buybacks are cut while capital is rebuilt and a Basel III endgame re-proposal lifts requirements.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A super-regional bank is valued on what it can distribute after funding its regulatory capital, discounted at a USD cost of equity -- never on statutory operating cash flow (loan and deposit movement) and never with deposits or borrowed funds treated as net debt. Core GAAP net income is the flow; capital retention at 10% of RWA growth is the reinvestment; preferred stock and NCI are deducted at book so the common claim is valued; 10.5% is the return an owner requires from a diversified, Category-III US bank with the 10-year Treasury at ~5%. The result is the residual-income answer in FCFE form: at an ~18-19% return on tangible common equity and 3.5-6.5% growth fading to 2.5%, PNC is worth ~2.2x tangible book (~$107.65) in the base case against the ~2.05x the market pays -- single-digit upside to the weighted value, a bear case roughly a fifth below the price, and a 15%-hurdle entry price far below today's quote. Most of the fall from the prior version is the corrected risk-free rate, not the Q3 results.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cost of equity: the 10.0% -> 10.5% correction is worth ~$18/share on the weighted value; each 50bp is ~7%. If the 10-year falls back toward 4.5% the prior values are the right ones

Net interest margin: 5bp on ~$575bn of average earning assets is ~$290m of NII (~1.1% of revenue, ~2.8% of NPAT); NIM fell to 2.94% in Q3 2026 and the base now leans on loan volume rather than margin, which costs capital

Credit cycle: every 10bp on the provision rate over ~$380bn of loans is ~$380m pre-tax (~3.7% of NPAT); net charge-offs rose to $257m in Q3 2026; office CRE ($4.8bn, 27.9% criticized, 10.8% nonperforming, 9.2% reserve) is the visible stress, the acquired FirstBank book and the fast-grown 2026 C&I vintage the unseasoned ones
Efficiency: the base assumes ~2.7pp of improvement from FY26E core 57.7% to 55.0% by FY2029; every 1pp is ~$280m pre-tax (~2.7% of NPAT), and FY2026 expense guidance has already been raised once

Capital: CET1 9.8% vs a 10% target and falling while buybacks continue; AOCI (-$6.5bn) is excluded by election. A Basel III endgame re-proposal, loss of the AOCI opt-out or credit-driven RWA migration would force retention above the modelled path and cut the ~$2.3bn/yr buyback
Share count: the ~1.0m Q4-to-date repurchase estimate is an approximation until the FY2026 10-K cover prints; each 4m shares is ~1% of value per share
SBC is estimated (~$300m) from Note 17 grant values because PNC does not disclose the expense; because it is added back and charged again in the engine, an error here moves value by only cents
Preferred stock is deducted at $5,357m carrying value; the economic value of the ~$290m/yr dividend stream at a 10.5% cost of equity is lower, so the bridge is ~$4/share conservative

Anchor refresh: fully diluted shares 397.7m -> 396.8m (14 Oct cover count less Q4-to-date buybacks)
Anchor refresh: preferred after Series S redemption + redemption cash + NCI (5,930 -> 5,939)

Driver change: FY2027-28 pre-tax margin lowered (expense guidance raised; base 41.3/41.5 -> 40.5/41.0, bull 42.5/43.5 -> 41.7/43.0) and base FY2027 capital retention 8.2% -> 10.0% of revenue (RWA growth)

bridge.note: ties to probability_weighted.weighted_iv; each step is a staged make build-dcf run (257.02 after anchors, 255.91 after drivers, 237.92 after the rate). Price move since the prior version does not enter the value.

inputs.base_revenue_definition: FY2026E CORE total revenue = net interest income + noninterest income (GAAP, not FTE), excluding integration costs and significant items as PNC defines them (Table 38 of the Q3 2026 10-Q: Visa exchange gain +$459m, Visa B-3 derivative -$121m, securities losses -$139m, integration costs in fee income -$16m; net +$183m in the first nine months). FY2026 ends 31 Dec 2026; nine months are reported. Build: 9M 2026 actual 19,602 GAAP (NII 12,274 + noninterest income 7,328) = 19,419 core; Q4 2026 ~6,841 on the 15 Oct 2026 guidance (NII +4.0% q/q on 4,206 = ~4,374; fee income +3.5% on Q3's 2,142 = ~2,217; other noninterest income ~$250m). Total ~26,260. Cross-check against the full-year guidance in the Q3 10-Q: total revenue ex-items +13.7% on FY2025 23,099 = 26,264 (NII +15.5% = 16,644; noninterest income ex-items +10.5% on 8,689 = 9,601). The prior version (2026-10-02) used 26,100 on the July guidance (+~13%); the October guidance raise is +0.6%. FY0 = FY2026E so year 1 = FY2027. The CSV Revenue column IS total revenue for PNC (us-gaap:Revenues), unlike HBAN/NTRS where it is the ASC-606 fee subset.
inputs.share_count_basis: 396,778,009 common shares outstanding at 14 Oct 2026 (Q3 2026 10-Q cover; equity statement shows 397m at 30 Sep 2026 after 2m repurchased in the quarter) LESS an ESTIMATED ~1.0m repurchased 14 Oct-19 Nov 2026 (Q4 repurchases guided to approximate Q3's ~$0.56bn; ~40% of the quarter elapsed at ~$215-225) PLUS ~1.0m dilutive awards (Q3 2026 basic EPS $4.98 vs diluted $4.97; basic and diluted weighted averages both round to 401m) = ~396.8m fully diluted at the valuation date. The prior version's estimate for 30 Sep (397.7m) was ~0.9m too high against the printed cover count. Held FLAT thereafter: share-based compensation is expensed in the flows, so charging dilution too would double-count, and buybacks are a distribution of the FCFE capitalised, not a separate driver. The ~13.9m shares issued for FirstBank (5 Jan 2026) are in the base. REFRESH from the FY2026 10-K cover (due late Feb 2027).
inputs.funding_note: Net debt is held at ZERO by construction. PNC is a Fed/OCC-regulated bank holding company: borrowed funds $79,757m and deposits $466,362m at 30 Sep 2026 are operating funding whose cost is already inside net interest income; interest-earning deposits with banks $24,670m (largely at the Fed) are liquidity held against that funding, not surplus cash. The flow capitalised is free cash flow to equity (net income less capital retained to fund risk-weighted-asset growth at the ~10% CET1 operating target) at the cost of equity, so no debt is deducted and no cash added. total_debt and cash are for audit only. Preferred stock is deducted at book in equity_bridge (see there for the Series S redemption); the flows are therefore total net income (before preferred dividends), NOT net income to common, so the preferred cost is charged exactly once.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2026E FCFE ~5,900, set equal to what PNC is actually distributing: common dividends ~2,990 (9M ~2,196 declared/paid + $2.00 x ~397m in Q4) + preferred ~310 + buybacks ~2,550 (9M 1,984 + ~570 guided for Q4) + ~50 other. Core net income is ~8,270 (26,260 revenue - ~15,150 core noninterest expense [guided +9.5% ex-items on 13,834] - ~840 provision [9M 590 + ~250] = ~10,270 pre-tax x (1 - 19.5%)), so ~2,370 is retained. That retention did NOT hold CET1 flat: organic loan growth of $30bn+ in nine months took RWA to $500.7bn and CET1 from 10.6% to 9.8% (FirstBank accounts for part of the fall), i.e. 2026 distributions ran ahead of the capital the growth needed. The forward capex_pct_path charges the full retention. GAAP FY2026E net income ~8,065 (9M actual 5,924). reported_fcf = FCFE + share-based compensation so that last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc_incl_equity_taxes - interest_income holds.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: Statutory operating cash flow (FY2025 4,384; FY2023 10,111; Q1 2025 -509) is loan/deposit/trading movement and meaningless as free cash flow for a bank; the CSV FreeCashFlow column is NOT used. reported_fcf here is the FCFE proxy before the SBC charge.
inputs.sbc_source: ESTIMATED: PNC does not tag us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensation and the 10-K Note 17 discloses no expense line. FY2025 10-K Note 17: 1.87m PSUs/RSUs granted at ~$191 (~$357m of grant value, ratable over ~3 years), $256m intrinsic value vested in 2025 ($214m 2024, $219m 2023); 5.27m nonvested units at ~$165 at 31 Dec 2025 (~$870m). Annual expense ~$300m = ~1.15% of FY2026E revenue. Taxes withheld on net-share settlement are inside the treasury-stock line and immaterial. SBC is already inside GAAP noninterest expense, so it is added back to the margin driver and charged again via sbc_pct_path -- net zero on the flow, band narrow.
inputs.interest_income_note: Not stripped: interest income IS the banking business, and no cash is added to equity value.
inputs.buyback_note: PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock $1,984m in the first nine months of 2026 ($796m Q1, ~$622m Q2, ~$566m Q3); Q4 2026 guided to approximate Q3. ~27% of the 100m-share authorisation remained at 30 Sep 2026. FY2025 $1,338m, FY2024 $687m, FY2023 $651m (CET1 rebuild after March 2023), FY2022 $3,731m. Buybacks are a use of the FCFE capitalised, not an extra source of value. Note the pace is being held with CET1 at 9.8%, below the ~10% operating target.
inputs.share_count_date: 2026-10-14 (Q3 2026 10-Q cover count, less estimated Q4-to-date repurchases)
inputs.book_value_anchor: Common shareholders' equity $56,474m at 30 Sep 2026 (BVPS $142.17, down from $145.52 at 30 Jun because AOCI fell $2,352m in the quarter to -$6,472m as bond yields rose). Tangible common equity ~$42,760m = common equity less goodwill net of deferred tax $13,085m and other disallowed intangibles $629m (Q3 10-Q capital table) = TBVPS ~$107.65 on 397.2m shares (derived here, not the company-reported figure; was $111.09 at 30 Jun). CET1 excludes AOCI by election: CET1 capital $49,138m on RWA $500,661m = 9.8% (9.9% at 30 Jun, 10.6% at 31 Dec 2025) against a ~10% operating target; Tier 1 11.0%. Q3 2026 ROE 13.89% (Q2 13.61%); ROTCE ~18% (estimated: annualised net income to common 2,006 over ~$43.6bn average tangible common). At the valuation-date price the market pays roughly 2.05x TBV and 1.56x book.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity in USD, the currency of the flows: 10-year US Treasury ~5.0% (5.07% on 18 Nov 2026; weekly closes 4.86-5.28% since mid-September) + beta 1.1 x US equity risk premium 5.0% = 10.5%. CORRECTION versus the 2026-10-02 version, which wrote the 10-year at '~4.5% (late September 2026)' and so used 10.0%: the 10-year actually closed at ~5.2-5.3% that week (Yahoo ^TNX), so the input was stale then and is ~55bp higher than modelled now. The formula is unchanged; only the risk-free input is corrected. The same rise is what took $2.35bn out of AOCI in Q3. Beta 1.1 sits below the 1.2 used for HBAN (2026-09-29) because PNC is roughly twice HBAN's size, less NIM-geared (fees ~37% of revenue), carries a Category III deposit franchise that held through March 2023, and has a measured five-year beta of ~1.0-1.2. One rate across all three scenarios; credit-cycle, CRE and capital-rule risk is charged in the bear flows and the 20% bear weight, not stacked as a premium. COHORT NOTE: HBAN and NTRS were valued in the same week as the prior PNC version and may carry the same stale risk-free input; PNC is no longer directly comparable with them until they are refreshed.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases (~2,400 branches) are immaterial relative to $64bn of equity; lease cost sits inside noninterest expense and therefore inside the modelled pre-tax margin. No lease line and no lease liability deduction.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests are trivial ($57m of equity at 30 Sep 2026; ~$60m/yr of net income, $45m in 9M 2026). They are deducted at book in equity_bridge; the ~$0.6bn capitalised value of their share of the flows is ~0.2% of equity value and is left inside the flows (noted, not modelled). The 19.5% cash-tax-rate driver is the guided FY2026 effective rate, reaffirmed in the Q3 10-Q (9M 2026 19.9% = 1,471/7,395; FY2025 17.5%).
inputs.notes: MODEL (unchanged from 2026-10-02): Bank FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity, run through the component engine (house precedent HBAN, NTRS, NAB.AX, IAG.AX, GL). SKILL.md routes a bank to residual income on tangible book; FCFE with retention = NPAT x g/ROTE is the clean-surplus equivalent, and it goes through the validated slider engine, which also produces the workbook. BVPS-compounding is NOT used: book value is ~24% goodwill/intangibles and swings with AOCI (-$6.5bn). Engine mapping: revenue = NII + noninterest income (core, GAAP); ebitda_margin_path = pre-tax income (revenue - noninterest expense - provision) PLUS share-based compensation, as % of revenue; sbc_pct_path = 1.15%; da_pct = 0 (depreciation and intangible amortisation are inside noninterest expense and are genuine costs for a bank); capex_pct_path = capital RETAINED to fund RWA growth at the ~10% CET1 target; cash_tax_rate_path = 19.5%; wacc = cost of equity; net_debt = 0; equity_bridge = preferred stock, the Series S redemption cash and NCI. THIS UPDATE (2026-11-19, after Q3 2026 results of 15 Oct and the Q3 10-Q): (1) anchors refreshed to 30 Sep 2026 -- price, share count from the 14 Oct cover, preferred/NCI, FY2026E revenue base 26,100 -> 26,260 on the raised guidance; (2) two driver years re-judged, FY2027-28 pre-tax margin (base 41.3/41.5 -> 40.5/41.0; bull 42.5/43.5 -> 41.7/43.0) and base FY2027 capital retention (8.2 -> 10.0); (3) cost of equity 10.0% -> 10.5% in all scenarios, a correction of the risk-free input (see wacc_rationale) and by far the largest mover. DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED: all growth paths (the Q3 NIM slip to 2.94% is offset by loan growth far above what was assumed -- the guided Q4 run-rate NII of ~4,374 x 4 is already +5.1% on FY2026E, so the base FY2027 NII +7.5% needs only ~2.3% on top; would move down if Q4 NII misses the +4% guide or NIM fails to reach ~3.0% by Q1 2027); FY2029+ margins (55.0% efficiency / 4.6% provision; would move if FY2027 core expense growth exceeds ~5% or NCOs run above ~30bp for two quarters -- they are 24bp for 9M 2026, 27bp in Q3 including $35m from the education-loan transfer); FY2028+ retention; the entire bear case (it already carries NIM stalling at ~2.95%, a credit cycle and a CET1 rebuild); SBC 1.15%; tax 19.5%; terminal growth; weights 20/50/30. FY2026E core anchor: revenue 26,260, core noninterest expense ~15,150 (GAAP ~15,555 incl. ~$265m of integration expense and the $140m Foundation contribution), provision ~840, core pre-tax 39.1% of revenue, core efficiency 57.7% (Q3 core 56.5%; Q4 guided ~57.1% as expense steps up 5% q/q). FY2027 base reconciliation: 26,260 x 1.065 = 27,967 revenue x (40.5% - 1.15%) x (1 - 19.5%) = ~8,860 net income, less ~290 preferred dividends (after the Series S redemption) and ~60 NCI = ~8,510 to common / 396.8m = ~$21.45 GAAP EPS (vs FY2026E GAAP ~$19.05 / core ~$19.75). Residual-income cross-check on tangible book: steady-state P/TBV = (ROTE - g)/(CoE - g) = (17.5 - 2.5)/(10.5 - 2.5) = 1.875x on tangible common + preferred (~$48.1bn after the Series S redemption) = ~$90.2bn, less preferred $5.4bn = ~$214/share. The engine base sits ~$23 above it (~2.2x common TBV, ~11x FY2027E EPS) because the steady-state formula ignores the FY27-FY31 phase in which revenue compounds at 3.5-6.5% at a ROTE ~7pp above the cost of equity. At 10.5% the market's ~2.05x TBV implies a steady-state ROTCE of ~19%, i.e. the price already embeds roughly the base FY2027 return. Price is the NYSE regular close of 18 Nov 2026, not an after-hours print. Q4 2026 results are due mid-January 2027; 30 Sep 2026 is the latest balance sheet. Qualitative items with no modelled effect: the Coinbase/USDC stablecoin payment pilot (Nov 2026; no disclosed economics) and the CFO handover to Alexander Overstrom by March 2027.

bear.growth_rationale: UNCHANGED path. The Fed cuts faster than the curve implies into a slowdown: asset yields reset while deposit competition (megabanks, high-yield online banks) keeps funding costs sticky, so NIM stalls at ~2.95% instead of breaking 3%; loan growth slows to 1-2% as borrowers de-lever; capital markets fees give back the 2026 pull-forward. Revenue +2% FY27, flat FY28, then 2-3% nominal. The Q3 2026 NIM of 2.94% is at this case's stall level; what keeps it a bear rather than the base is that NII is still guided +4% q/q on volume.
bear.margin_rationale: UNCHANGED path. FY27: efficiency 58.0% (revenue shortfall against a largely fixed cost base; the $350m cost programme offset by technology/compliance) - provision 6.5% (~45bp: office CRE -- 27.9% criticized and 10.8% nonperforming on a $4.8bn book at 30 Sep 2026, 9.2% reserved -- migrating into the broader $36bn CRE book, plus seasoning of the acquired FirstBank loans) + 1.15 = 36.6. FY28 credit cycle: provision 10.0% (~70bp; FY2020 COVID was 3,175 = 18.8% of revenue, so this is a mid-sized cycle, not a crisis) with efficiency 59.0%: 32.1. FY29 provision 7.0%, efficiency 58.5%: 35.6. Recovers to provision 6.0% (~42bp) and efficiency 58.0%: 37.1, held -- no operating leverage. FY27 EPS ~$18.5, FY28 ~$16; ROTCE ~13-15%.
bear.capex_rationale: UNCHANGED. Retention = NPAT margin ~29% x RWA growth / ROTE ~14% = ~2.1 x g. FY27-29 held at 5.5-6.0% despite 0-2.5% growth because RWA migration in a downturn, a Basel III endgame re-proposal and rebuilding CET1 from 9.8% to the 10% target (~$1.0bn on $500.7bn of RWA) consume capital the model must top up (the 2023 precedent was a buyback cut to ~$650m/yr, not a raise). FY30 6.3% at 3% growth; terminal 2% growth retains 4.2%.

base.growth_rationale: UNCHANGED path. Total core revenue. FY27 6.5%: NII ~+7.5% and fees +5%. The composition has shifted since the prior version: NIM slipped 2bp to 2.94% in Q3 2026 (growth in lower-yielding, higher-quality commercial loans; higher funding costs) rather than marching through 3.00%, but average loans grew 2% q/q in Q3 and are guided +2.5% in Q4 with NII +4.0%, so the Q4 run-rate (~4,374 x 4 = ~17,500) is already +5.1% on FY2026E NII of ~16,650. FY27 NII +7.5% therefore needs ~2.3% above the exit run-rate -- more volume, less margin than first assumed, which is why FY27 capital retention is raised instead. Fees: Q4 guided run-rate ~9,870/yr (fees 2,217 + other 250, x4) vs FY2026E core 9,600; +5% in FY27 needs ~2% on top. No further acquisition effect: FirstBank closed 5 Jan 2026 and is in FY0 for the full year. FY28 5.0% as the repricing tailwind fades; tapers to 2.5% terminal, bracketing the 3.0% and 6.5% 3/5-year revenue CAGRs.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-tax income + SBC on revenue. FY26E core: 100 - efficiency 57.7% - provision 3.2% = 39.1% (+1.15 SBC = 40.3). CHANGED FY27 41.3 -> 40.5 and FY28 41.5 -> 41.0 on the expense evidence: FY2026 core expense guidance was raised from +8.5% to +9.5% in October, and Q4 2026 core expense is guided +5% q/q to ~3,910, an annualised ~15,640 that is already 3.2% above FY2026E. The prior FY27 efficiency of 55.7% needed core expense +~3%, i.e. below the Q4 run-rate. FY27 now 40.5 = 100 - efficiency 56.6% (core expense +4.5% on revenue +6.5%: still ~1pp of positive operating leverage from the $350m continuous-improvement programme and FirstBank synergies) - provision 4.1% (~30bp on ~$390bn average loans; NCOs 24bp for 9M 2026, guided ~$250m/quarter = ~26bp) + 1.15. FY28 41.0 = efficiency 55.8% - provision 4.3% + 1.15. UNCHANGED FY29+ 41.5 = efficiency 55.0% - provision 4.6% (~33bp mid-cycle) + 1.15, held: the destination stands, the glide is a year slower. FY2025 actual was 36.7% pre-tax + ~1.2% SBC on a 59.9% GAAP efficiency ratio.
base.capex_rationale: Capital retained to hold CET1 at ~10% as RWA grows = 10% x change in RWA (equivalently NPAT margin x balance-sheet growth / ROTE, ~1.83 x g). CHANGED FY27 8.2 -> 10.0: RWA reached $500.7bn at 30 Sep 2026 (+~2.6% in the quarter) and average loans are guided +2.5% again in Q4, so RWA exits 2026 near $510bn growing at a high-single-digit annualised rate, not the GDP-like rate the prior version assumed for the second half. FY27 RWA growth is taken at 5.5% (was 4.5%): ~$28bn x 10% = ~$2.8bn = 10.0% of FY27 revenue (~32% of NPAT retained -> ~68% distributed = $8.00 dividend ~$3.2bn + preferred ~$0.3bn + ~$2.5bn of buybacks, about the current pace). It does NOT add the ~$1.0bn needed to lift CET1 from 9.8% back to 10.0%: management is holding the buyback pace at 9.8%, and that rebuild is charged in the bear case. UNCHANGED FY28+: 8.2% at 4.5% RWA growth, stepping down with growth to 4.6% at the 2.5% terminal rate (~14% retained).

bull.growth_rationale: UNCHANGED path. NIM reaches ~3.20% by FY28 as fixed-rate assets reprice and the 10-Q's 'risks skewed toward tighter monetary policy' play out for an asset-sensitive balance sheet; Denver/Phoenix (FirstBank) and the BBVA Sunbelt markets take deposit share; commercial loans grow 6-7%; capital markets compound toward management's 25-30% target. Revenue +8% FY27 fading to 3% terminal. Q3 2026 evidence cuts both ways for this case: C&I loans +4% q/q supports the volume leg, the 2bp NIM slip on lower-spread growth argues against the 3.20% margin leg.
bull.margin_rationale: CHANGED FY27 42.5 -> 41.7 and FY28 43.5 -> 43.0 for the same expense run-rate evidence as the base (Q4 2026 core efficiency guided ~57%): FY27 = efficiency 55.4% - provision 4.0% + 1.15 = 41.7; FY28 = 54.1% - 4.0% + 1.15 = 43.0. UNCHANGED FY29+: positive operating leverage takes efficiency to 52.5% by FY30 (peers USB/FITB run ~55-57%, money-centres mid-50s) with credit benign at ~4.0% of revenue (~28bp): 100 - 52.5 - 4.0 + 1.15 = 44.6, held. FY27 EPS ~$22.5, ROTCE ~20%.
bull.capex_rationale: UNCHANGED. Retention = NPAT margin ~35% x RWA growth / ROTE ~20% = ~1.75 x g: higher growth needs more capital even at a better return. FY27 at 6% RWA growth retains 10.5% of revenue (~30% of NPAT); FY28 5.5% -> 9.6%; terminal 3% growth retains 5.3% (~15%).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: UNCHANGED at 20/50/30 (house default 15/50/35). Q3 2026 evidence is mixed and does not move the weights: against -- CET1 slipped again to 9.8% with buybacks continuing, AOCI fell $2.35bn, NIM dipped 2bp and net charge-offs rose to $257m (27bp; +44% y/y, $35m of it the education-loan transfer); for -- full-year revenue and NII guidance was raised, EPS beat, nonperforming loans are 0.58% of loans (0.67% at year-end) and office criticized eased to 27.9% (nonperforming rose to 10.8%, 9.2% reserved). Bear stays at 20% rather than the 25% used for HBAN/NTRS because PNC raised guidance and its integration is complete; it would go to 25% if CET1 falls below ~9.5% or NCOs run above ~35bp. Bull stays at 30%: the base already credits ~3% NIM, the $350m cost programme and continued capital-markets strength.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
